question.worked_solution:
First, we express

$$
f(x)=-4(\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))^{5}.
$$

Now, we see that $f(x)$ can be expressed as the composite function

$$
f=-4{u}^{5},\,u=\operatorname{cos}⁡(x).
$$

Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}=-20{u}^{4},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-\operatorname{sin}⁡(x).
$$

We now apply the chain rule, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =-20{u}^{4}\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)) \\  & =20{cos}^{4}⁡(x)\operatorname{sin}⁡(x).\end{aligned}
$$
